title: A Clean Account
summary: Lead an Aurelian custody detachment through a disputed repossession. Secure records and service routes with superior weapons, then decide what duty requires when the people behind the inventory become impossible to ignore.

opening.title: An orderly return
body: Quartermaster Ada Rusk is on Apron Seven with a stalled service cart, a crated optic and a custody warrant that will not move either of them. Your four bright walkers have just left the Tender. Beyond the surveyed lane, local machines wait in the ravines with none of your calibration records and an excellent knowledge of the ground.

The Continuance needs inherited roots for failing civil-defence machines elsewhere. You command its best-equipped claim detail, but replacement optics are finite and repairs come out of the company account. Clear Rusk's approach, preserve what she is carrying and make a warrant useful to the people who must carry it through the next gate.

chapters.title: Rusk’s long optic
body: Rusk brings the service cart aboard herself. Its Focused Large Laser enters your stores against a signed recovery receipt, not a claim on the defeated cordon. She sets it beside a Halberd's arm mounts: the same weight and fitting boxes as a Large Laser, more reach, more heat in each discharge and a slower cycle.

At Cutbank's two posts, a fixed gun watches Sarn Avenue while local crews move through the gardens. A saved Long Watch refit can use Rusk's optic to support the approach. The emitter cannot see through stone or protect an exposed side; the detachment still has to earn a firing position. An optional survey and tender recovery remain available for supplies.

chapters.title: The parts that arrived
body: The tender's loading stand survives and the transfer is complete. Its emitters were existing stock, allocated because your detachment reached them. No factory has started making roots again. Your quartermaster's advice is blunt: use the advanced equipment where it earns its place, and keep a compatible local gun when it gets a machine back into service.

chapters.title: Saye’s two signatures
body: Registrar Len Saye keeps the two original repair rolls flat under a sheet of glass while your clerks copy them. They carry different serials and the same fitter's signature. The difference is an offence in the warrant and a history of continued work in Saye's account. He insists on accompanying both copies to Sarn Registry Court.

Its temporary loadway admits 175 tonnes. All four of your opening machines total 205, so someone stays with the Tender. A heavy firing line and a lighter detail with fast eyes are both possible. The next order protects a record through a short transfer; it does not require hunting every defender into the workshops.

chapters.title: The cost of an inventory
body: Saye reaches the copied inventory with both originals still under glass. The workers who attacked the court have names in those rolls. Rusk notes which machines the company kept in reserve and what it spent protecting the copy. Superior equipment secured the ground; it did not make the decision free.

A route between the civil service readers can establish which serials belong to which roots. The next warrant asks for a small verification detail. Carry the evidence forward and leave the district enough witnesses to explain it.

chapters.title: Borrowed numbers
body: The relay chain shows workshops sharing the least-disputed serials to keep different surviving roots in service. They copied records, not machines. The Authority sees fraud; the yards describe the paperwork that kept pumps, haulers and walkers working after the Foundry Winter. Blackglass Quarry holds the plates and receipts that can establish how far the practice went.

chapters.title: The people in the account
body: Blackglass's ledger, lift manifest and serial punch survive. The record traces copied numbers back to working repair yards rather than a hidden walker factory. The next warrant covers their live power conduit. Your company is still required to secure it. It now knows what will stop working if the eventual export order is carried through.

chapters.title: One remaining signature
body: The conduit is held long enough for its records to be checked. Barrow Yard keeps the master warrant beside the local repair compact. Both have surviving witnesses. Securing that archive may settle more than the route of a shipment: it will establish whether Continuance custody must mean removing a working root from Tessell.

chapters.title: What the warrant permits
body: Barrow supports two lawful outcomes. Export sends disputed roots to reinforce failing Continuance civil defence and closes Tessellan yards that rely on them. Countersigned stewardship keeps the machines here under named maintenance obligations and leaves shortages elsewhere. Neither creates a root or cancels the other claim.
The final operations are alternative endings. Export uses the freight corridor; stewardship uses the public and service sides. The commander must choose which cost the detachment will own.

chapters.title: The shipment closes
body: The export register is sealed. Continuance settlements will receive inherited roots their service works cannot replace. Tessellan fitters watch the same machines leave the yards that kept them alive. The detachment fulfilled a lawful warrant and recorded its full cost instead of hiding it beneath a clean total.
Arne calls the shipment duty done. Silas keeps the closure list attached to the report. Petra submits both. The account balances only because it refuses to pretend that nothing was lost.

chapters.title: A different form of custody
body: The Tender countersigns local stewardship. The roots remain on Tessell, with the workshops named as keepers and their service history preserved. The Continuance’s need remains real. The detachment declined to meet it by closing these yards, and its report must explain what other settlements will do without the shipment.

Petra carries the signed record home. Silas supplies the argument, Teodor the operational cost and Arne a formal dissent that remains part of the account. Duty now means maintaining the decision after the guns are quiet.
